title: Forgeblock Finance SOC 2 / ISO27001 posture & Trust Center mapping sync
summary: Introductory posture review focused on SOC 2 and ISO 27001 evidence access, RBAC/SSO integration, KMS/bring-your-own-key, and EU data residency requirements. Agreed next steps: share SOC 2 report and evidence map, grant temporary Trust Center viewer access, and schedule a technical KMS integration session + a short perf benchmark for their POC workloads.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. I'm Maya on Redwood's account team, with Ethan our SE. Quick soundcheck?
[00:14] Lina (Forgeblock): Hi, Lina here, can hear you. Marcus here as well.
[00:18] Marcus (Forgeblock): Yup, all good.
[00:21] Ethan (Redwood SE): Great. We'll run through posture, trust center access, and then dig into KMS and logs. We know you flagged EU residency and SOC two reporting — sorry, SOC 2 here.
[00:36] Priya (GRC): Yes, our auditors want to see evidence flows and we need to map controls to our existing control matrix. Also curious about RBAC — we use Okta and SAML.
[00:45] Maya: Perfect. Quick agenda: 1) what you need for SOC 2/ISO audit, 2) how Redwood's Trust Center and evidence artifacts map, 3) technical touchpoints (SSO, RBAC, KMS), 4) next steps. Sound OK?
[00:56] Tom (Audit Lead): Sounds good. Timeline note: our audit window starts mid-Jan, so we need access and sample evidence by early December ideally.
[01:05] Ethan: Noted. On evidence access we can grant a Trust Center viewer role that gives read access to reports, control mappings, and logs extracts. We don't share raw production data but we provide the artifacts auditors generally need.
[01:22] Lina: Can you clarify what you mean by "artifacts"? Are those full reports, screenshots, or downloadable log batches?
[01:30] Ethan: Good question. Artifacts are a mix: PDF attestation (SOC 2 type II), control narratives, configuration screenshots, exportable audit logs (redacted token IDs), and KMS configuration docs. Downloads depend on your plan — hosted customers get standard exports, dedicated/private can request longer retention snapshots.
[01:49] Marcus: We are in AWS eu-west-1, using EKS and some serverless. Data residency is non-negotiable; only EU regions for customer data. How does Redwood ensure that?
[02:02] Maya: Redwood supports region pinning at the tenant level — we can route inference to EU-hosted capacity. For Redwood Dedicated or Private you can keep everything in your VPC. For Hosted, we do have EU regions and can set routing policies.
[02:18] Priya: Okay, and logs — retention policy? Our compliance requires 12 months of immutable logs for certain controls.
[02:26] Ethan: Default hosted logging retention is 90 days in the UI, with exports. For audits we provide archived extracts; for 12+ months we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with extended retention add-on or integrating logs into your SIEM via the event export API.
[02:44] Lina: Is the event export real-time stream or batch? We want tamper-evident transport.
[02:50] Ethan: We support both. There's a near real-time webhook/stream and scheduled monthly batch exports. For tamper evidence we sign exports and you can push them to your KMS-encrypted S3 bucket.
[03:03] Marcus: On KMS — do you support BYOK (bring your own key) with HSM-backed keys? We have strict key management requirements.
[03:11] Ethan: Yes, we support BYOK with customer-managed keys in AWS KMS. For Private deployments we can integrate with on-prem HSMs or your KMS via a direct peering or customer-managed connector. There are some limits on tokenization of the keys for hosted, but full BYOK is supported on Dedicated/Private.
[03:28] Tom: Any audit evidence that shows encryption-at-rest and key rotation? Our policy wants rotation logs and proof of separation of duties.
[03:37] Ethan: We can include key rotation logs, KMS access IAM roles, and separation-of-duty mappings from the Trust Center. We also have syslog exports that show KMS API calls and who invoked them.
[03:50] Priya: We use privileged access reviews quarterly; can you show RBAC roles mapping to our SSO groups?
[03:58] Maya: We can map Redwood roles to SAML groups from Okta. The Trust Center has an RBAC matrix export that lists role names, permissions, and sample users.
[04:09] Lina: Is it possible to restrict who can download raw logs? We want only auditors to pull them, not devs.
[04:16] Ethan: Yes — RBAC can restrict export permissions. We support fine-grained permissioning so only roles with "AuditExport" can download log bundles. That's configurable via SAML attribute mapping.
[04:30] Marcus: I want to understand differences between hosted and dedicated for our use-case. If we stay hosted but pin to EU, are there any control gaps that would prevent us from meeting SOC 2?
[04:42] Ethan: Hosted in EU can meet SOC 2 controls functionally, but there are operational differences: retention limits, control over key lifecycle (BYOK limited), and audit SLA. For guaranteed 12-month immutable logs and full BYOK with HSM, Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[04:59] Priya: Do you have a compliance playbook or control mappings we can overlay on our matrix?
[05:06] Maya: Yes, we'll share a control mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 / ISO 27001 clauses. That will include where evidence is located in the Trust Center.
[05:16] Tom: Great. Also, how do you handle subprocessor disclosures and vendor attestations for data processing?
[05:22] Maya: We provide a subprocessors list in the trust center and our DPA. For vendor attestations, the SOC 2 report includes subservice org disclosures as applicable.
[05:33] Lina: On SSO, we use Just-In-Time provisioning in Okta. Can Redwood consume SCIM or just SAML?
[05:41] Ethan: We support SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning for user/group sync. JIT in Okta will still work for SSO flows but SCIM helps populate groups and automate role assignment.
[05:53] Marcus: For the POC, we plan to route low-latency inference through a hosted endpoint. Can you provide a short perf benchmark and cost estimate focused on EU region?
[06:03] Ethan: Absolutely. We'll run a 24-hour benchmark on a sample model with your sequence lengths and provide latency P95, throughput, and estimated per-token costs. Do you have a sample prompt set?
[06:13] Marcus: We'll share a small set — maybe 500 queries.
[06:17] Ethan: Perfect. We'll need an API key scoped to a staging tenant.
[06:20] Speaker 3: (murmur)
[06:23] Priya: Back to evidence: you mentioned signed exports — who signs them? 
[06:27] Ethan: Our export signing service uses Redwood's signing key; we include a signature file and a checksum. For Dedicated we can configure your own signing key or push signed artifacts directly into your key-wrapped bucket.
[06:41] Lina: Is there a way to preview the Trust Center as an auditor with limited permissions so they can't drop configs?
[06:48] Maya: Yes — we can create an "Auditor" role limited to read-only access and no ability to trigger configs or download sensitive raw payloads unless you explicitly permit it.
[06:59] Tom: About evidence retention, the auditors might request server configs from six months ago. How granular are snapshots?
[07:07] Ethan: Snapshots capture config state and control evidence at the time of snapshot; default cadence is weekly for hosted, daily for Dedicated. For historic snapshots beyond retention window we can provide archived snapshots on request for a fee.
[07:24] Marcus: Any limitations around exporting KV cache or model caches for debugging? We sometimes need token-level traces for latency incidents.
[07:33] Ethan: We never export raw user content by default. For debug sessions we provide redacted traces or we can run on anonymized sample data under a controlled process with NDAs. Token-level KV cache dumps are sensitive; we'd only do that in Private or Dedicated under strict controls.
[07:53] Priya: Can you show an example of the RBAC matrix?
[07:57] Maya: We'll attach a sample in the follow-up email. It lists roles like Admin, AuditViewer, ModelDeploy, EndpointOperator with columns for allowed actions.
[08:08] Lina: For ISO 27001, do you have Statement of Applicability (SoA) style mapping?
[08:13] Maya: Yes — our control mapping includes SOC 2 and ISO clauses with evidence locations. It's not a full SoA but it provides the traceability your auditor usually wants.
[08:24] Tom: Regarding proof of separation of duties, can you export IAM role change logs?
[08:29] Ethan: Yes, change logs and who approved them are available via the audit log exports.
[08:35] Marcus: Any blockers integrating our KMS cross-account? We're thinking about a cross-account IAM role in AWS for KMS invocations.
[08:44] Ethan: Cross-account KMS is supported; we provide docs for the IAM trust policy and the key policy changes. For hosted there are more guardrails, but for Dedicated we'll assist with role setup during the integration session.
[08:58] Priya: Ok last security question — pen test results and vulnerability disclosures?
[09:03] Maya: We publish a high-level summary and will share redacted pentest findings in the Trust Center. For sensitive details we can get into an NDA exchange.
[09:13] Tom: Timeline recap: we need artefacts in early December and a technical KMS session before Nov 25. Is that doable?
[09:22] Maya: Yes — we can share SOC 2 and the control map by Nov 16, grant Trust Center auditor viewer by Nov 18, and set a KMS integration deep-dive for Nov 23 or 24. Ethan, are you able to run the benchmark by Nov 30?
[09:36] Ethan: Yes, benchmark + cost estimate completed by Nov 30 if we get the prompt set and staging creds this week.
[09:44] Lina: Great. Anything else?
[09:46] Marcus: No, this was helpful.
[09:48] Maya: Thanks all. We'll follow up with the attachments and calendar invites.
[09:52] [end of captured transcript — approximate. Transcription includes occasional mislabels and filler words. Some technical terms like "KV cache" were transcribed as "K V cash" in places. ]
